persona: Independent simulated first-time RILL beginner interested in a small electronic dance groove.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: The empty-lane MIDI hint, instrument assignment, pencil tool and one-click Duplicate made a complete arrangement possible with the mouse. Precise trimming took a retry and playback needed setup recovery.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark interface, teal waveforms and colored piano-roll notes look clean and musical. At the zoom needed for 30 seconds, every repeated pattern title became the same truncated New p... label.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Note drawing, duplication, naming and MIDI export responded promptly. WAV export showed an elapsed-time progress notice before success. This is a session impression, not a hardware or latency benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Most tool descriptions explained the next gesture. Initial playback failed with System default output, and a short trim movement did not visibly change the duration; choosing the available output and using a larger snapped trim recovered both.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: I found audio and MIDI arrangement, a VST3 instrument, piano-roll drawing, duplication, exact duration feedback, a mouse keyboard for naming, project saving and both requested exports. Only one laboratory instrument was available, and broader production features were not evaluated.

findings.observation: Double-clicking beneath the audio lane, as the visible hint suggested, opened Device library. Assign instrument created a MIDI pattern with Rill Lab Sine visibly assigned.
Double-clicking the MIDI pattern opened the piano roll. Pencil showed Draw notes / Drag to set length, and four mouse drags produced visible C4, E4, G4 and E4 notes.
The Duplicate tool said Click a clip to duplicate. Clicking successive audio and MIDI clips appended copies, allowing the arrangement to grow without keyboard shortcuts.
The first audio trim ended at 30.134 seconds. After changing Snap to 1 bar, a five-pixel drag still left 30.134 visible; an eight-pixel held drag then displayed End 30.000 s and Duration 4.286 s.
The first Play attempt left the playhead at the start and displayed Audio output stream failed or disconnected.
Audio setup showed System default output. Selecting Rill lab paced output, applying and pressing Play produced a Pause button, later playhead movement to 004.03.18, and visible meters on both tracks.

File / Rename project exposed a Keyboard button. Its on-screen keys, Select all and Space let me enter neon step entirely by mouse; Save proposed neon step.rill in session-2, and accepting returned to an unmarked project title.

WAV export identified Arrangement 0:30. I unchecked Include effect tails, accepted neon step.wav in the session-2 picker, and saw Exported / neon step.wav. MIDI export similarly proposed neon step.mid and showed its success notice.
At the zoom needed to see the whole 30-second piece, the repeated MIDI clip names all displayed as New p..., making individual clips hard to distinguish by title.

outcome.status: Completed according to the visible UI: 30.000-second arrangement, project saved, and WAV and MIDI export success notices observed. File content verification remains with the coordinator.
outcome.composition: 112 BPM, 4/4. Startup Circuit rhythm audio copied to three full four-bar clips plus a final two-bar clip. A one-bar C4/E4/G4/E4 figure was drawn and duplicated across fourteen bars in a Rill Lab Sine MIDI track.
outcome.playback_observed: First playback reported an output-stream failure. After changing the visible output selection, the playhead advanced from the start to 004.03.18 and both track meters lit. Stopped playback afterward. No audio was auditioned.

limitations: Only assigned screenshots and supplied mouse driver were used for composition; no source, project contents or other participant records were inspected.
No file contents or heard audio claim; export paths and success were observed in the UI, with independent coordinator verification to follow.
The virtual laboratory output and software graphics do not establish physical audio latency or sound quality.
Only the installed laboratory Rill Lab Sine VST3 was used; other plug-ins were not evaluated.
Elapsed session time includes tool, screenshot and reporting overhead and is not a benchmark.
